summary: 1. The new 25-Sep-24-Oct fiscal month opens on Sep 25 at -20.53% against its half-day Friday target, but ore beats its own target for the first time in nine days. 2. Total landed at 8,649 BCM against a 10,883.6 BCM target, with waste running 26.05% under target and ore running 34.67% over it, a reversal after eight straight ore-target misses through the end of September. 2. 3. The 26-Sep HOD meeting independently calls Sep 25 "a red production day, approximately 23,000 tones, around 6,700 tones below plan," within about 700 t of the workbook's own variance, and pins roughly 5,000 t of the loss on equipment downtime, chiefly EX-262's extended service and hose leak and EX-263's new A/C fault. 3. 4. On the fleet side, EX-327 opens a Hydraulic Oil Leaking breakdown, the longest single stoppage in the day's report, while EX-123 and EX-253 both extend their own standing multi-day stoppages to four and ten days respectively, and WL-101's Accident Damage record, open since 01-Feb-26, finally closes after roughly 236 days. 5. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 6. The formal EOM sign-off for the closed 25-Aug-24-Sep cycle gives a Total Pit Mined Volume of 593,309 BCM, reading 99.12% of the 598,598 BCM monthly target — 9,899 BCM above the INX-SUM workbook's own running survey total for the same cycle (583,410 BCM, 97.46%). 7. The sign-off's own signature date reads "August 25, 2026," a date that predates the cycle it closes; worth a direct check with the survey team on whether that is a template artifact. 8. See [[survey-volume-reconciliation]]. 9. EX-123's replacement part status needs confirming today. The HOD meeting reports a part "reportedly ordered from Germany with 7-10-day ETA" but flags that management wants documented proof of the order, the supplier confirmation, and a firm ETA — the unit has now been down four full days. If the 7-10 day window holds, EX-123 stays down into early October, overlapping the 4-11 October Maaden crusher-shutdown excavator loan already on the books. See [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. The October workbook's populated tab is mislabeled. It carries the header "Sept (24)" but its own date cell reads Friday 2026-09-25, meaning every subsequent tab in the series may run one day offset from its label. Worth flagging to the team producing the workbook so the day-25 pass does not misread a tab. DT-107 and DT-128 both remain down on matching Engine Coolant Temperature High faults, now on their second and eighth consecutive days respectively; the HOD meeting says DT-128's engine installation is targeted for completion by the afternoon of 27-Sep. No new daily INX-SUM survey workbook landed this pass — the newest file remains `260925-INX-SUM.xlsx`, already registered and compiled in the prior pass as Sep 24 data under the standing publishing-lag pattern. The next daily reading, covering Sep 25, is due on the next pass. Source: `Production report/Oct 26/October Client Meeting Report-.xlsx` (Sep 25 data); `Maintanance Shedules/Oct 26/DailyAvailability_Final_Report (25-09-2025 ).pdf`; `HOD Meetings/HOD Morning Meeting 26 Sep 26.msg`; `Survey Data/Sep 26/eom report sheet_sept_2026_signed.pdf`. `October Block Info.xlsx`, `October A & U.xlsx`, `DPR-October-2026.xlsx`, `October Daily Drill Meters Report-.xlsx`, `Daily Drill Sampling Record-2026.xlsx`, `DPR and A&U- October-2026.docx`, `Equipment running hours report -.xlsx`, and `Grade Control Sheet October 2026.xlsx` registered, cross-check only. `October Distance Report-.xlsx`'s newly populated "Sep (25)" tab registered, cross-check only, flagged for a future distance-focused pass. Tasks: none created this pass. The EX-123 parts-confirmation item and the tab-mislabeling flag are logged as open questions in the affected articles rather than dispatched as action items. Important References, Notes & References, and Task Feedback Log workflows were not run this pass, per the task's own instructions. No content removed or renamed from RAW. ---
